purpose: Reviewed OpenStreetMap geometry anchors for Lineside layout reconciliation. Not a runtime data source.

source.coverage: Reading east throat to Maidenhead and the Twyford corridor
source.query_summary: railway=signal nodes and railway=rail ways; selected named siding ways and the Kennet Bridge four-track cross-section fetched with full geometry

signal_position_audit.display_version: v1/v2 shared fixed-grid renderer as reviewed 2026-08-16
signal_position_audit.method: Compared OSM longitude separations for the five named Up Main signals with their current SVG dot positions. The dots are attached to the exit edge of the corresponding berth cell.
signal_position_audit.finding: The displayed dot spacings do not preserve the physical relative spacings, so they must not be used as a cross-line geographic reference until the layout uses projected OSM/path coordinates.
signal_position_audit.safe_interpretation: Signal state, direction and berth-boundary association remain valid. Only their displayed geographic spacing is unvalidated.
signal_position_audit.required_before_promotion: Place each row on projected path coordinates or along-track chainage, then retain each signal dot at its established berth exit boundary. Do not infer unlabelled signal locations from TD signal bits alone.

review.learner_route: 1665 -> 1669 -> 1677 is the dominant Down Relief path; 1669 -> 1679 -> 1687 is the sparse long-dwell branch.
review.geometry_finding: The mapped loop is a continuous approximately 0.7 km road. It must not be drawn as a short local V or hump between adjacent berth cells.
review.rendering_status: The temporary v2 loop is only an occupancy separation. A surveyed/projection-based long-loop drawing remains required before promoting v2.
review.shared_smart_label: SMART resolves both 1669 and 1679 to KEN BG LP. The 3150 normal-flow, 31.5-second samples for 1669 versus 36, 424-second samples for 1679 distinguish the physical loop berth from the through berth.

limitations: OSM signal refs identify physical geometry anchors only; they do not identify Network Rail SF address/bit mappings.
Do not auto-accept OSM edits or infer unmapped TD berth positions from an adjacent OSM line without learner and SMART evidence.
A named OSM siding can still form the observed TD route; its OSM service classification must not be used to discard a high-confidence TD transition.
For Kennet Loop, use the full three-way geometry and a coordinate projection before changing the visual route again.
This compact snapshot intentionally contains reviewed anchors, not a full live OSM extract.
